title: Etale presentation test for intrinsic stack local quasi-finiteness
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Locally of finite type for stacks is tested on smooth scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with the scheme notion [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; finite type means locally of finite type and quasi-compact, where quasi-compactness is tested on the point spaces of base changes by affine schemes. The point space $|\mathcal X|$ consists of field-valued [def-weil-field] objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. A stack morphism is locally quasi-finite if it is locally of finite type, its relative diagonal is locally quasi-finite (tested on scheme charts using [pqf-def-quasifinite]), and every field fibre has discrete point space. An etale scheme chart is a representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale morphism from a scheme; an atlas is a surjective chart. Etale uses [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts. For a morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$, the following conditions are equivalent. (a) $f$ is locally quasi-finite in the intrinsic sense just specified. (b) For every scheme $V\to\mathcal Y$ and every etale scheme chart $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, the composite scheme map $U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]; the chart $U$ need not be surjective. (c) There exist an etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$ and an etale scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ such that $U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 06UF (lemma-characterize-locally-quasi-finite), conditions (1), (2), (4), specialized to DM etale presentations; Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM) and Tag 06UC (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field). Intrinsic definition: Tag 06PU (definition-locally-quasi-finite).

proof.text: Assume (a), and fix $V\to\mathcal Y$ and a chart $U\to\mathcal Z=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ as in (b). The DM atlas calculus makes $\mathcal Z$ DM. Base change in the finite-type calculus makes $\mathcal Z\to V$ locally of finite type. Apply the chartwise calculus to the representable-by-algebraic-spaces map $U\to\mathcal Z$: it is etale, hence smooth, hence locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type. These implications are applied only to the chart, not to $f$. Composition in the stack finite-type calculus and its compatibility with the ordinary scheme notion make $U\to V$ locally of finite type.

For every field map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$, write $\mathcal Z_k=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its point space is discrete by (a), and its structure map is locally of finite type by base change. The base-changed chart $U_k=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal Z_k$ is etale. Apply the field-chart lemma to conclude that $U_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite, hence locally of finite type. Now let $u\in U$ with image $v\in V$ and take $k=\kappa(v)$, so that $U_k$ is the scheme fibre $U_v$. The fibre of $U_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ over its unique point is all of $U_k$, so the point-isolation lemma applied to $U_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that every point of $U_v$, in particular the point over $u$, is isolated in $U_v$. By Step 1 the scheme map $U\to V$ is locally of finite type; choose affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R\ni v$ of $V$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A\ni u$ of $U$ mapping into it. The isolated-fibre-point lemma, applied to $U\to V$ at $u$, gives that $R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of $u$, which is quasi-finiteness of $U\to V$ at $u$. As $u$ was arbitrary, this proves (b). No surjectivity of $U$ was used.

Assume (b). Choose an etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$, then an etale scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, which exists by DM fibre-product closure. Apply (b) to these charts to obtain (c).

Assume (c), and denote the displayed scheme map by $h:U\to V$. A locally quasi-finite scheme map is locally of finite type. The two etale atlases $V\to\mathcal Y$ and $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ are representable by algebraic spaces, so the etale-implies-smooth clause of the current chartwise calculus applies to each. Both are surjective by (c). The current finite-type calculus explicitly tests local finite type on a smooth scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$ and a smooth scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$, independently of the chosen presentation. Apply that clause to these two smooth surjections and the locally finite-type scheme map $h$ to conclude that $f$ is locally of finite type. Independently, the relative diagonal lemma gives that $\Delta_f$ is locally quasi-finite. It remains to check discreteness of every field fibre.

Fix $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal Y$ and put $\mathcal X_k=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $P=V\times_{\mathcal Y}\operatorname{Spec}k$. The DM atlas calculus gives an etale scheme atlas $W\to P$. The map $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale surjective by base change, so $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is etale. Set $T=U\times_VW$. To verify that $T$ is an atlas of $\mathcal X_k$, put $Q=\mathcal X_k\times_kP$. Projection to $\mathcal X_k$ and $P$ gives a map $Q\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$. Its base change of $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is $U\times_VP\to Q$: an object on either side of the asserted identification is an object of $U$, an object of $P$, and an isomorphism between their images in $V$; the remaining $\mathcal X$-object and its isomorphism are determined up to unique isomorphism by the $U$-object. The same description identifies arrows. Now $T\to U\times_VP$ is the base change of $W\to P$, and $Q\to\mathcal X_k$ is the base change of $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. These three maps are etale surjective by the atlas calculus; their composite $T\to\mathcal X_k$ is therefore an etale surjective scheme atlas.

The etale map $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite (apply the etale-space lemma with the identity scheme chart), hence locally of finite type; its fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is all of $W$, so the point-isolation lemma makes every point of $W$ open, and $|W|$ is discrete. Since $T\to W$ is the base change of $h$, it too is locally quasi-finite, hence locally of finite type. For $t\in T$ over $w\in W$, the point-isolation lemma shows that $\{t\}$ is open in the subspace given by the preimage of $w$. That preimage is open in $T$, being the inverse image of the open singleton $\{w\}$. Thus each point of $T$ is open, and $|T|$ is discrete. For any subset $A\subseteq|\mathcal X_k|$, its inverse image in the etale surjective scheme atlas $T$ is open. The atlas description of the point-space topology therefore makes $A$ open. This proves that $|\mathcal X_k|$ is discrete. Together with the preceding finite-type and diagonal assertions this gives (a) and completes the equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem locallyQuasiFinite_moduli_iff_etale_atlas {S : Scheme.{u}} {F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)} {G : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)} (hF : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack F) (hG : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack G) (f : BasedFunctor F G) : (IsLocallyQuasiFiniteModuliMap f ↔ ∀ (V : Over S) (v : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj V)) G) (U : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct v f)) (p : U ⟶ V), IsEtaleModuliMap a → Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (a.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst v f)) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map p))) → Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite p.left) ∧ (IsLocallyQuasiFiniteModuliMap f ↔ ∃ (V : Over S) (v : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj V)) G) (U : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) (moduliTwoFiberProduct v f)) (p : U ⟶ V), IsEtaleModuliAtlas v ∧ IsEtaleModuliAtlas a ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (a.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst v f)) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map p))) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite p.left)
